title: AVGO: long a de-rated AI compounder at ~13.5x FY28 consensus; target $390, research target (12m) $407, stop $261
call_reason: The published 12-month target ($390.49) is above the $349.57 price, conviction is medium, and there is no special situation; the supervisor's 8% cap limits size and the book gets 2 shares.
one_liner: Broadcom has fallen ~30% from its June high while earnings rose ~43%. It trades at ~13.5x LSEG FY28 EPS of $25.86, against management's $115B FY27 / $230B FY28 AI roadmap. We underwrite consensus EPS, not management's >$30, and still get a $407 research target (12m) (+16%) and a $390 target (+12%, P(gain) 60%), with the Q4 print on ~Dec 10 as the first test.

thesis.point: Earnings are compounding faster than the stock is falling: the de-rating is multiple, not fundamentals.
thesis.evidence: Q3 FY26 revenue $29.6B (+86% y/y), AI semis $16.7B (+221%), non-GAAP EPS $3.32, FCF $13.7B. The Q4 guide is $34.8B with $21.7B AI. Yet the stock is back at its end-2025 level with EPS ~43% higher and ~30% below the June high, at ~18x FY27 consensus ($19.38) and ~13.5x FY28 ($25.86).

thesis.point: We do not need management's numbers: consensus EPS at a below-peer multiple gets to ~$407.
thesis.evidence: Management guides $115B FY27 and $230B FY28 AI revenue and >$30 FY28 EPS; LSEG consensus is $25.86. All five agents value on NTM EPS of $24.7-26.5 at 16.5-17x, i.e. at or below consensus. Every $1 of FY28 EPS the market underwrites is worth ~$16-17/share, so each beat on the path toward >$30 is upside to the target.

thesis.point: The XPV financing scare is smaller than the headline: expected loss ~$0.5/share.
thesis.evidence: The 10-Q (Note 10) shows a Backstop of one customer's 5-year lease obligations: 85% of lease balance owed less rack resale value, max ~$29B, fair value not material, nothing paid, plus a facility under which the customer may issue Broadcom up to $42B of convertible notes (none issued). BofA's $370B is a hypothetical 20 GW build-out; its loss case on the existing tranche is ~$2.9B. We deduct ~$2-2.5B (~$0.5/share).

variant_view: The variant view is modest, and it cuts both ways. Against the options market we are more constructive: its implied 12-month median is ~$364 with P(gain) 54%, while our blended target is $390 with P(gain) 60%, because the agents give credit for ~2x EPS growth at a compressed ~16-17x NTM multiple that the market is not paying for today. Against the sell side we are far more cautious: 38 analysts rate it Strong Buy with a median target of $525.5 (mean $517), which in effect capitalizes management's >$30 FY28 EPS at ~18-20x. We underwrite LSEG's $25.86 and a discount for six-customer concentration, Google's move toward MediaTek and the XPV overhang. So this is not a contrarian call. It is a 'consensus earnings, de-rated multiple' call that is roughly half-way between options pricing and the Street.

valuation.methods: The research target (12m) of $407 is the mean of five independent agents ($391-425), valued as of Sep 2027. Legs: (1) P/E on NTM (mostly FY28) EPS of $24.7-26.5 at 16.5-17x = $420-439 (40-60% weight); (2) FCF yield of 5-5.5% on ~$97-122B NTM/FY28 FCF = $388-441; (3) DCF at 10% WACC, 3% terminal growth = $311-373 (agents 1 and 5); (4) SOTP with AI at 16x after-tax earnings = $333-388 (agents 2 and 3). EV-based legs deduct $35.4B net debt ($59.419B debt less $23.975B cash) and ~$2-2.5B expected XPV loss; all use 4.94B non-GAAP diluted shares. $407 is ~16x NTM EPS of ~$25.5, dividends (~$2.60/yr) excluded. The published $390.49 target is the median of the blended distribution (67% options market, 33% agents after calibration), below the research target (12m) because of the 44-58% volatility and the fat left tail. Expected value is $435; quartiles $291 / $522.

catalysts.event: Micron fiscal Q4 FY26 results (after close)
catalysts.why_it_moves: HBM pricing and supply read-through: memory-heavy XPUs are the main reason Broadcom's gross margin is guided down to ~73%, and HBM/substrate tightness can shift XPU revenue across quarters.
catalysts.watch: HBM4 pricing for 2027, sold-out commentary and capacity adds; higher HBM prices are bullish for AI demand but negative for AVGO gross margin.

catalysts.event: Anthropic public S-1 / institutional roadshow / possible IPO pricing
catalysts.why_it_moves: Anthropic is expected to be Broadcom's largest XPU customer in 2027 and the tenant behind the XPV lease Backstop (max ~$29B) and the $42B convertible-note facility. A funded, well-received IPO de-risks both the 5 GW TPU ramp and the credit overhang; a delay or weak pricing does the opposite. The S-1 will also disclose the size and terms of the compute commitments.
catalysts.watch: Public S-1 filing; disclosed compute commitments to Google/Broadcom and the Fluidstack/XPV leases; pricing versus the $965B Series H mark; any delay announcement.

catalysts.event: Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon Q3 results and first 2027 capex guides
catalysts.why_it_moves: Google TPU and Meta MTIA spending is Broadcom revenue. 2027 capex growth is expected to slow from ~79% to ~35%; a weaker guide would hit the multiple, a stronger one would support the $115B FY27 plan.
catalysts.watch: 2027 capex ranges, Alphabet TPU commentary (Broadcom vs MediaTek), Meta MTIA scale-up, any mention of data-center power/shell delays.

catalysts.event: China SASAC decision on Broadcom switches in state-backed data centres
catalysts.why_it_moves: The survey found Broadcom switches in up to ~90% of state-owned data centres and is also examining bundling. Informal 'domestic chips' guidance would cut China networking sales and add an antitrust-style overhang.
catalysts.watch: Reports of informal procurement guidance favouring Huawei/H3C/Ruijie, any SAMR bundling probe, and management quantifying China switch exposure.

catalysts.event: XPV follow-on debt deal (~$70-80B, reported) for Anthropic/OpenAI compute
catalysts.why_it_moves: Pricing and demand for the next tranche is the market's cleanest read on XPV credit risk; a new tranche also enlarges Broadcom's contingent exposure.
catalysts.watch: Deal size, spread, Broadcom's Backstop terms on the new tranche, rating-agency and credit-strategist commentary.

catalysts.why_it_moves: Sector sentiment on AI capex; AVGO has traded with the group since the September 'pace the frontier' sell-off.
catalysts.watch: Data-center guide versus the $108B revenue outlook; comments on customer ASIC competition and power constraints.

catalysts.event: Broadcom Q4 FY26 results, FY27 outlook and annual dividend increase (after close; date from aggregators, not yet announced by Broadcom)
catalysts.why_it_moves: The first hard checkpoint on the $115B FY27 AI plan. The Q3 print fell despite a beat because the Q4 guide was light; this print sets the Q1 FY27 guide and the tone for the $230B FY28 target.
catalysts.watch: Q4 AI revenue vs $21.7B guide and total vs $34.8B; Q1 FY27 AI guide (needs a run-rate consistent with ~$29B/quarter average for $115B); explicit reaffirmation of $115B/$230B and >$30 FY28 EPS; gross margin vs ~73%; XPV Backstop balance and any convertible notes issued; Google share comments; dividend raise.

catalysts.event: Hyperscaler Q4 results and finalized 2027 capex budgets
catalysts.why_it_moves: Locks in the capex envelope that funds FY27 XPU and networking shipments.
catalysts.watch: Year-over-year 2027 capex growth versus the ~35% expectation; Google TPU generation vendor split.

catalysts.why_it_moves: First quarter of the FY27 ramp: shows whether the Anthropic TPU 8i (5 GW) and OpenAI (1.3 GW) deployments start on schedule.
catalysts.watch: AI revenue run-rate versus the $115B path, gross margin trend, 10-Q update on XPV Backstop and note-facility draws.

risks.risk: Frontier-lab deployment or funding slip (Anthropic, OpenAI) pushes FY27 AI revenue well under $115B and turns XPV into a live credit issue.
risks.signpost: Anthropic IPO delayed or priced well below the Series H mark; OpenAI stays private into late 2027; any convertible notes issued under the $42B facility in a 10-Q; management softening '$115B' to timing language on land/power/shell readiness.

risks.risk: Google moves TPU volume to MediaTek faster than Macquarie's 95% -> 80% -> 65% (2026-28) path.
risks.signpost: Alphabet or supply-chain reports of MediaTek winning next-gen TPU volume; Broadcom declining to quantify Google revenue for FY27; further sell-side FY28 EPS cuts.

risks.risk: The multiple compresses further on AI-capex digestion fears (the 12-20x range explains most of the outcome spread).
risks.signpost: 2027 hyperscaler capex growth guided below ~35%; a renewed 'pace the frontier' policy push; the stock closing below the $289.96 52-week low while estimates hold.

risks.risk: Gross-margin dilution and China: memory-heavy XPUs/racks and a SASAC substitution push.
risks.signpost: Gross margin guided below ~73% for Q1 FY27; formal or informal SASAC procurement guidance against Broadcom switches.

trade.position: 2 sh (~$699, 7.0% of the $10,000 book); size limited by the supervisor's 8% cap
trade.entry: Two tranches: half now, half after the Q4 FY26 report (expected 2026-12-10), or earlier on a close below ~$300 with the FY27/FY28 AI targets reaffirmed. The share ladder adds to 3 sh at ~$318 and trims to 1 sh at ~$360.
trade.exit_or_add: Exit on a close below $261 (thesis break, ~10% under the 52-week low, ~13.5x FY27 EPS) or on a cut to the $115B FY27 AI plan. Add, up to the 8% cap, after a clean Q4 print that reaffirms $115B/$230B, or on a drop to ~$300-318 with the roadmap intact. Trim toward 1 sh above ~$360 without new information; take profit at $522.

what_changes_our_mind: The Q4 FY26 print (~Dec 10) guides Q1 FY27 AI revenue below a run-rate consistent with $115B, or management stops reaffirming the $230B FY28 target.
Anthropic's IPO is pulled or priced sharply below its $965B private mark, or a 10-Q shows convertible notes issued under the $42B facility or a payment under the lease Backstop.
2027 hyperscaler capex guides (late Oct / early Feb) come in flat to down, or Alphabet confirms a majority of next-gen TPU volume moving to MediaTek.
